Start free Key Takeaways The global privacy management software market reached roughly $6.24 billion in 2026, up from $5.07 billion in 2025, per Mordor Intelligence’s Privacy Management Software Market report (updated 14 May 2026). A second tracker, Fortune Business Insights, scoping the category as data privacy software, puts 2026 at $7.54 billion , up from $5.37 billion in 2025. Mordor Intelligence forecasts the market to reach $17.63 billion by 2031 (23.08% CAGR); Fortune Business Insights forecasts $60.40 billion by 2034 (29.70% CAGR). North America holds the largest regional share at 37.60% of 2025 revenue per Mordor Intelligence, with Europe second at 28.80% and Asia-Pacific the fastest-growing region at a 27.2% CAGR . Investors poured $9.4 billion into cybersecurity and privacy-focused startups in the first half of 2025, the strongest half in three years, led by Cyera’s $540 million Series E. OneTrust held 29.7% of the data privacy compliance software market, more than double its nearest competitor, per the most recent IDC breakdown publicly disclosed (2022). The global privacy management software market reached roughly $6.24 billion in 2026, up from $5.07 billion in 2025 , according to Mordor Intelligence’s Privacy Management Software Market report, last updated 14 May 2026. That figure covers software vendors selling consent management, data mapping, subject-request automation, and compliance tooling to organizations that process personal data. A second tracker scopes the category slightly differently and lands on a higher number, but both agree spending is accelerating faster than most adjacent enterprise software categories. Vendor revenue is only half the story. The other half is where that money is coming from: regulatory expansion, AI governance bolted onto existing privacy programs, and a fresh wave of venture funding chasing data-protection startups. Below is the market size by tracker, the growth curve, the regional and vendor landscape, and the funding flowing into the sector. How big is the global privacy tech market in 2026? Two independent research firms publish 2026 estimates for this category, and they differ because they scope the market differently. Mordor Intelligence puts the global privacy management software market at $6.24 billion in 2026 , up from $5.07 billion in 2025. Fortune Business Insights, which labels the same broad category “data privacy software” and includes a slightly wider band of compliance and data-protection tooling, puts 2026 at $7.54 billion , up from $5.37 billion in 2025. Mordor Intelligence’s narrower scope tracks closer to core consent, data-mapping, and compliance-workflow software, while Fortune Business Insights folds in a broader band of data-protection tooling, which produces a higher headline number and a steeper long-run forecast. How fast is the privacy tech market growing? Mordor Intelligence projects a 23.08% compound annual growth rate from 2026 to 2031, taking the market from $6.24 billion to $17.63 billion, nearly tripling in five years. Fortune Business Insights projects a steeper 29.70% CAGR from 2026 to 2034, reaching $60.40 billion over a longer eight-year window. A longer forecast window and a wider category scope both push the compounded end figure higher, so the two percentages are not directly comparable without accounting for the different time horizons. Which region and industry lead privacy tech spending? North America holds the largest regional share of privacy tech revenue, at 37.60% in 2025, per Mordor Intelligence, reflecting the concentration of both large enterprise buyers and the leading vendors headquartered in the United States. Europe is second at 28.80% , driven by GDPR and the EU AI Act creating overlapping compliance requirements that push organizations toward integrated platforms rather than manual processes. Region 2025 revenue share Growth outlook Primary driver North America 37.60% (largest) Steady growth as the installed base CCPA/CPRA and state privacy law expansion Europe 28.80% Steady, compliance-driven demand GDPR and EU AI Act overlap Asia-Pacific Smaller base 27.2% CAGR (fastest) New national privacy laws, rising digitalization Table sourced from Mordor Intelligence, Privacy Management Software Market (updated 14 May 2026). Asia-Pacific is the fastest-growing region rather than the largest one, expanding at a 27.2% CAGR as new national privacy laws take effect across the region and Mordor Intelligence notes the region “is expected to close the gap by 2031.” By functionality, consent and preference management is the largest slice of spend at 30.60% of the market, and by deployment, cloud and SaaS delivery accounts for 66.30% , both per Mordor Intelligence’s segment breakdown. Who are the leading privacy tech vendors? OneTrust, TrustArc, Securiti, BigID, and SAP are named as the leading vendors across both trackers reviewed for this post, alongside a wider bench that includes Microsoft, IBM, Cisco, Collibra, Informatica, Exterro, and WireWheel. Mordor Intelligence describes the market as showing “moderate concentration,” with established platforms facing sustained challenges from AI-focused entrants and accelerating consolidation as buyers favor integrated suites over point products. That 29.7% figure is dated: it is the most recent breakdown IDC has published with a specific percentage, and OneTrust has since been named a Leader in both the Forrester Wave for Privacy Management Software (Q4 2025) and the IDC MarketScape for Data Privacy Compliance Software (2025) without either firm publishing a refreshed market-share number alongside those rankings. Treat 29.7% as the last confirmed data point rather than a current one. How much venture capital is flowing into privacy tech? Investors poured $9.4 billion into cybersecurity and privacy-focused startups in the first half of 2025 alone, according to Crunchbase News, split between $4.5 billion in the first quarter and $4.9 billion in the second, the strongest six-month stretch in three years. That figure blends cybersecurity broadly with privacy-specific deals rather than isolating privacy tech alone, so treat it as an upper-bound signal of investor appetite in the adjacent category rather than a privacy-only total. Figure 4: Funding and market-size milestones line up in the same window. Sources: Crunchbase News (16 July 2025), Mordor Intelligence (14 May 2026), Fortune Business Insights (13 July 2026). The single largest round was AI-enabled data security platform Cyera’s $540 million Series E, closed in the second quarter of 2025 at a $6 billion valuation and led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Georgian, and Greenoaks. At least 11 rounds of $100 million or more closed for security and privacy startups in that quarter alone, a concentration of capital in fewer, larger, later-stage deals rather than a broad spread across new entrants. What is driving privacy tech spending in 2026? Two forces are compounding on top of the baseline regulatory pressure that has funded this category since GDPR: AI governance and platform consolidation. Organizations that already run a privacy compliance stack are extending it to cover AI training data and model outputs rather than buying a separate AI governance tool, and organizations operating across multiple jurisdictions are consolidating point solutions into fewer, broader platforms. Figure 5: The two decisions that route an organization toward enterprise platform spend versus a lighter compliance stack. Source: Mordor Intelligence market driver analysis (2026 edition), Crunchbase News funding-focus commentary (2025). Cloud-native delivery reinforces both trends: 66.30% of privacy tech revenue is already cloud or SaaS delivered, per Mordor Intelligence, which lowers the switching cost for a buyer consolidating three point tools into one platform compared to a decade ago, when on-premises deployments made migration slower and more expensive. The Bottom Line Whichever tracker’s total is cited, the privacy tech market crossed well over $6 billion in 2026 and is compounding at 23% to nearly 30% a year depending on scope, a growth rate few adjacent enterprise software categories are matching. North America and Europe hold the installed base today, Asia-Pacific is where new deployments are concentrating fastest, and OneTrust’s last confirmed near-30% market share signals a moderately concentrated field rather than a fragmented one. For a site owner or founder watching this from outside an enterprise budget, the underlying lesson is not that privacy compliance requires a six- or seven-figure platform: the same disclosure requirements these platforms automate for large buyers, current cookie and data-sharing language, consent logging, and a jurisdiction-aware privacy policy, still have to be met, and a generator built for that base layer closes the gap without the enterprise price tag.
